subject: cn
title: CN 2: Data Link Layer & Error Control

options.text: Padding a frame with zeros to reach the minimum frame size
Appending parity bits to each byte of the payload
Inserting a 0 after five consecutive 1s so data cannot imitate the frame delimiter
Adding idle bits between frames to maintain synchronisation

questions.explanation: The flag pattern 01111110 must be unique, so the transmitter inserts a 0 after any run of five 1s in the data and the receiver removes it. This is transparency, not padding.

questions.prompt: A bit-stuffing protocol uses the delimiter 01111110. If the stuffed output bit string is 01111100101, what was the input?
questions.explanation: Scanning the output, after the run 11111 the next 0 was inserted by the stuffer and is removed. Deleting that single bit from 01111100101 recovers the original 0111110101.

questions.prompt: Which property must a CRC generator polynomial G(x) have in order to detect all errors affecting an odd number of bits?

options.text: G(x) must have (x + 1) as a factor
G(x) must have a constant term of 0
G(x) must have degree at least 16

questions.explanation: An error pattern with an odd number of 1s is not divisible by x + 1, so if x + 1 divides G(x) no such pattern can divide G(x) either, and every odd-weight error is caught.

questions.prompt: A CRC scheme uses the generator polynomial x^3 + x + 1 (that is, 1011). For the message 11000, what are the three check bits appended?
questions.explanation: Append three zeros to give 11000000 and divide by 1011 modulo 2. The remainder of that division is 011, which becomes the check sequence.

questions.prompt: A binary code has the four valid code words 00000, 01011, 10101 and 11110. What is the minimum Hamming distance p, and how many bit errors q can be corrected?
questions.explanation: The closest pair of code words differs in three positions, so p = 3. A code corrects up to floor((p-1)/2) errors, which is 1.

questions.prompt: Frames of 1000 bits are sent over a 10^6 bps link with a one-way propagation time of 25 ms, using a sliding window that keeps the link fully packed. What is the minimum number of bits needed for the sequence number field?
questions.explanation: Transmission time is 1000/10^6 = 1 ms and the round trip is 50 ms, so up to 51 frames can be outstanding. Representing a window of 51 requires ceil(log2(51+1)) = 6 bits.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum sender window size for the selective repeat protocol with n-bit sequence numbers?
questions.explanation: Selective repeat needs the sender and receiver windows to be disjoint in sequence space, so each may be at most half the space, giving 2^(n-1). Go-back-N can use 2^n - 1 because its receiver window is one.

questions.prompt: Using stop-and-wait, a 3000-bit frame is sent at 2000 bps with a one-way propagation delay of 100 ms. Acknowledgements and processing are negligible. What is the channel utilisation?
questions.explanation: Transmission time is 3000/2000 = 1.5 s and the round trip adds 0.2 s. Utilisation is 1.5 / 1.7, which is about 88.2 percent.

questions.prompt: In stop-and-wait ARQ, which scenario gives the LOWEST link utilisation?

options.text: A short frame on a low-bandwidth link with a short propagation delay
A long frame on a low-bandwidth link with a short propagation delay
A short frame on a high-bandwidth link with a long propagation delay
A long frame on a high-bandwidth link with a short propagation delay

questions.explanation: Utilisation is transmission time divided by transmission plus round trip time. A small transmission time against a large propagation delay makes that ratio tiny: the sender spends nearly all its time waiting.

questions.prompt: How many check bits are required to detect two-bit errors and correct single-bit errors in a 16-bit data word using a Hamming code?
questions.explanation: Single-error correction on 16 data bits needs r with 2^r >= 16 + r + 1, satisfied at r = 5. Adding an overall parity bit for double-error detection makes 6 in total.
